attributes.action: Introduce laws requiring consent to film strangers and publish videos of them
attributes.additional_details: Being in public should not mean consenting to being filmed and exposed online. Identifiable footage can be shared without permission, leading to harassment, humiliation, reputational harm and AI misuse. This is particularly concerning for women and vulnerable people, including those filmed during arrests or medical emergencies. Recording incidents as evidence should remain lawful, but this should not automatically permit public posting. People should have control over how their image is used.
attributes.background: We want the Government to introduce laws requiring consent before publishing identifiable footage of strangers online, even if legally recorded. Also restrict deliberate, intrusive filming, including with wearable cameras. Exempt crowds, incidental appearances and justified public-interest uses.
